source.text: Ἐκέλευσε δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου στεφάνους ἐνεχθῆναι. καὶ ἐνέχθησαν στέφανοι ὡσεὶ ἐκ φοινίκων γεγονότες, καὶ ἐστεφάνωσε τοὺς ἄνδρας τοὺς ἐπιδεδωκότας τὰς ῥάβδους τὰς ἐχούσας τὰς παραφυάδας καὶ καρπόν τινα καὶ ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πύργον. 2. καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους δὲ ἀπέστειλεν εἰς τὸν πύργον, τοὺς τὰς ῥάβδους τὰς χλωρὰς ἐπιδεδωκότας καὶ παραφυάδας ἐχούσας, καρπὸν δὲ μὴ ἐχούσας τὰς παραφυάδας, δοὺς αὐτοῖς σφραγῖδας. 3. ἱματισμὸν δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν πάντες εἶχον λευκὸν ὡσεὶ χιόνα, οἱ πορευόμενοι εἰς τὸν πύργον. 4. καὶ τοὺς τὰς ῥάβδους ἐπιδεδωκότας χλωρὰς ὡς ἔλαβον ἀπέλυσε, δοὺς αὐτοῖς ἱματισμὸν καὶ σφραγῖδας. 5. μετὰ τὸ ταῦτα τελέσαι τὸν ἄγγελον λέγει τῷ ποιμένι· Ἐγὼ ὑπάγω· σὺ δὲ τούτους ἀπολύσεις εἰς τὰ τείχη, καθὼς ἄξιός ἐστί τις κατοικεῖν. κατανόησον δὲ τὰς ῥάβδους αὐτῶν ἐπιμελῶς καὶ οὕτως ἀπόλυσον· ἐπιμελῶς δὲ κατανόησον. βλέπε, μή τίς σε παρέλθῃ, φησίν, ἐὰν δὲ τίς σε παρέλθῃ, ἐγὼ αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον δοκιμάσω. ταῦτα εἰπὼν τῷ ποιμένι ἀπῆλθε. ἄγγελον λέγει μοι ὁ ποιμήν· Λάβωμεν πάντων τὰς ῥάβδους καὶ φυτεύσωμεν αὐτάς, εἴ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν δυνήσονται ζῆσαι. λέγω αὐτῷ· Κύριε, τὰ ξηρὰ ταῦτα πῶς δύνανται ζῆσαι; 7. ἀποκριθείς μοι λέγει· Τὸ δένδρον τοῦτο ἰτέα ἐστὶ καὶ φιλόζωον τὸ γένος· ἐὰν οὖν φυτευθῶσι καὶ μικρὰν ἰκμάδα λαμβάνωσιν αἱ ῥάβδοι, ζήσονται πολλαὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν· εἶτα δὲ πειράσωμεν καὶ ὕδωρ αὐταῖς παραχέειν. ἐάν τις αὐτῶν δυνηθῇ ζῆσαι, συγχαρήσομαι αὐτῇ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ζήσῃ, οὐχ εὑρεθήσομαι ἐγὼ ἀμελής. 8. ἐκέλευσε δέ μοι ὁ ποιμὴν καλέσαι καθὼς τις αὐτῶν ἐστάθη. ἦλθον τάγματα τάγματα, καὶ ἐπεδίδουν τὰς ῥάβδους τῷ ποιμένι. ἐλάμβανε δὲ ὁ ποιμὴν τὰς ῥάβδους, καὶ κατὰ τάγματα ἐφύτευσεν αὐτάς, καὶ μετὰ τὸ φυτεῦσαι ὕδωρ αὐταῖς πολὺ παρέχεεν, ὥστε ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος μὴ φαίνεσθαι τὰς ῥάβδους. 9. καὶ μετὰ τὸ ποτίσαι αὐτὸν τὰς ῥάβδους λέγει μοι· Ἄγωμεν, καὶ μετ' ὀλίγας ἡμέρας ἐπανέλθωμεν καὶ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τὰς ῥάβδους πάσας· ὁ γὰρ κτίσας τὸ δένδρον τοῦτο θέλει πάντας ζῆν τοὺς λαβόντας ἐκ τοῦ δένδρου τούτου κλάδους. ἐλπίζω δὲ κἀγὼ ὅτι λαβόντα τὰ ῥαβδία ταῦτα ἰκμάδα καὶ ποτισθέντα ὕδατι ζήσονται τὸ πλεῖστον μέρος αὐτῶν.

translation.text: Then the angel of the Lord commanded that crowns be brought[a]. And crowns were brought, as if made from palms, and he crowned the men who had handed in the rods that had shoots and some fruit, and he dismissed them into the tower. 2. And the others also he sent into the tower—those who had handed in their rods green and having shoots, but whose shoots did not have fruit—giving them seals. 3. And all who were going into the tower had the same clothing, white as snow. 4. And those who had handed in their rods green, just as they had received them, he dismissed, giving them clothing and seals. 5. After the angel had finished these things, he says to the shepherd: “I am going; but you are to dismiss these to the walls, as each one is worthy to dwell. Pay close attention to their rods, and so dismiss them—pay close attention. See that no one slips past you,” he says; “but if anyone does slip past you, I will test them upon the altar.” Having said these things to the shepherd, he went away. 6. The shepherd says to me, “Let us take the rods of all and plant them, to see if any of them will be able to live.” I say to him, “Sir, how can these dry things live?” 7. Answering me he says, “This tree is a willow, and its kind loves life. If, then, the rods are planted and receive a little moisture, many of them will live; then let us also try pouring water on them. If any of them is able to live, I will rejoice over it; but if it does not live, I shall not be found negligent.” 8. Then the shepherd commanded me to call them just as each of them had been stationed. Rank by rank they came and were handing their rods to the shepherd. The shepherd took the rods and planted them according to the ranks; and after planting he provided much water for them, so that because of the water the rods could not be seen. 9. And after he had watered the rods, he says to me, “Let us go, and after a few days let us return and inspect all the rods; for the one who created this tree desires all who have taken branches from this tree to live. And I too hope that, these rods having received moisture and having been watered with water[f][e][d][c][b], the greater part of them will live.”

footnotes.text: Crowns “as if made from palms” echoes Greco-Roman victory/festival wreaths; palm branches commonly signified triumph.
“Seals” in Hermas often resonate with baptismal sealing and divine ownership; the translation keeps the literal term to preserve the symbolism.
“To the walls … to dwell” situates people within the tower’s structure in the allegory; elsewhere in Hermas the tower represents the community being built.
The willow (ἰτέα) readily takes root from cuttings when given moisture, reinforcing the image of life restored by watering.
“Rank by rank” renders τάγματα τάγματα, a phrase of orderly, almost military grouping.
“Test upon the altar” retains the cultic image of evaluation in a sacred setting rather than a generic examination.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Formulaic genitive construction in early Christian Greek; retains idiom without over-interpreting as a theophany.
Stephanos denotes a victor’s wreath/crown; “crowns” is familiar while preserving reward/victory connotation.
Foînix commonly denotes the date-palm; “from palms” is concise and keeps the material image.
Consistent term throughout Similitude 8 for the distributed pieces from the willow; “rod” fits size and symbolism.
Agricultural term for new growth; “shoots” is clear, concrete, and standard botanical English.
Retains evaluative metaphor of moral productivity recurring in Hermas.
ἀπολύω in narrative scenes often means dismiss; here it signals being sent on to the tower/walls.
Common mission/transfer verb; “sent” is plain and accurate.
Standard rendering; preserves potential baptismal/ownership imagery without over-interpretation.
Collective sense of attire is in view; “clothing” communicates uniform appearance.
Idiomatic comparison; retains vividness and intertextual resonance without forcing NT phrasing.
Refers to the structural walls associated with the tower allegory; “walls” is straightforward.
Dwell carries ecclesial/eschatological nuance fitting placement within the tower.
Reproduces the doubled emphasis on careful scrutiny without redundancy overload.
Conveys the idea of evading scrutiny; idiomatic in English.
Maintains evaluative/judicial nuance, especially in cultic context with altar.
Cultic term; “altar” is sufficient and traditional without expansion.
Here a polite form of address to the shepherd-angel, not a divine title; “Sir” prevents theological confusion.
Botanical identification; “willow” is standard and connects to the rooting imagery.
Idiomatic rendering that preserves the personified characterization of the species.
Refers to life-giving wetness; “moisture” keeps the horticultural sense.
Captures the act of supplying water without over-technical spatial nuance.
Military/orderly grouping metaphor; “rank by rank” conveys repeated τάγματα τάγματα.
Plain agricultural verb; “plant” is natural English.
Highlights generous provision of water rather than the act of pouring alone.
Objective visibility is in view; “be seen” is simple and accurate.
Active scrutiny of the rods is intended; “inspect” conveys that.
Agent-defining participle; indefinite expression preserves focus on the act, not the title.
Standard arboreal term; “branches” contrasts with the cut “rods.”

theological_decisions.issue: Meaning of σφραγῖς (seal) in this context
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render literally as “seals,” leaving the symbolic referent (e.g., baptismal sealing, divine ownership, eschatological protection) implicit.
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas often uses “seal” imagery in baptismal contexts, but here the narrative distributes seals alongside clothing and crowns. Retaining “seals” preserves the polyvalence and allows readers to trace the symbolism across the work.
In vocative polite address to a non-divine interlocutor, “Sir” matches idiomatic Greek usage and avoids conferring divine title on the shepherd-angel.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy: contested terms—κύριος default is “Lord,” with context-driven variance documented.

theological_decisions.issue: “The one who created this tree desires all … to live” (v. 9)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Translate straightforwardly, preserving the universal desire without importing systematic conclusions.
alternative_readings: Qualify as “desires that as many as possible … live”
Paraphrase as “wills to give life to all who took branches”
theological_decisions.rationale: The line expresses the benevolent will of the creator within the allegory (the willow and its branches/rods). Preserving the breadth keeps Hermas’s exhortational tone toward repentance and life without resolving broader soteriological debates.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Doctrine philosophy: preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.

theological_decisions.rationale: The altar is part of Hermas’s symbolic temple/church imagery. Retaining it keeps the cultic register and gravity of examination.

theological_decisions.issue: “Angel of the Lord” capitalization and identification
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Lowercase “angel of the Lord” as an angelic envoy, not a theophany; retain genitive construction.
alternative_readings: Capitalize as a title (“Angel of the Lord”)
Render “angel from the Lord” to avoid genitive-of-possessor nuance
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas regularly features designated angels (e.g., the shepherd) as emissaries. Lowercase keeps narrative role clear without theological overstatement.

review_passes.summary: The draft is highly accurate and captures the narrative flow well. A few minor adjustments were made to resolve redundancies (e.g., 'watered with water', 'pay close attention... carefully'), smooth awkward phrasing with object complements ('the rods green' -> 'their rods green'), and align with established lexical decisions ('dismissed' for ἀπέλυσεν in v. 1).
issues_found: In v. 1, `ἀπέλυσεν` was translated as 'sent', missing the lexical decision to use 'dismissed' (which distinguishes it from `ἀπέστειλεν` in v. 2).
In v. 2 and 4, 'the rods green' is slightly awkward English for the object complement; 'their rods green' flows better.

In v. 5, 'Pay close attention to their rods carefully' double-translates `ἐπιμελῶς` and conflicts with the lexical decision's goal of avoiding redundancy. Revised to 'Pay close attention to their rods...'.
In v. 6, 'whether any of them will be able to live' (`εἴ τινες...`) is improved to 'to see if any of them...' for natural English flow after 'plant them'.
In v. 8, 'furnished much water' is slightly clunky for `παρέχεεν`; 'provided' is more natural.
In v. 9, 'watered with water' (`ποτισθέντα ὕδατι`) is redundant in English; 'watered' is sufficient.

The shepherd says to me, “Let us take the rods of all and plant them, to see if any of them will be able to live.” I say to him, “Sir, how can these dry things live?” 7. Answering me he says, “This tree is a willow, and its kind loves life. If, then, the rods are planted and receive a little moisture, many of them will live; then let us also try pouring water on them. If any of them is able to live, I will rejoice over it; but if it does not live, I shall not be found negligent.” 8. Then the shepherd commanded me to call them just as each of them had been stationed. Rank by rank they came and were handing their rods to the shepherd. The shepherd took the rods and planted them according to the ranks; and after planting he provided much water for them, so that because of the water the rods could not be seen. 9. And after he had watered the rods, he says to me, “Let us go, and after a few days let us return and inspect all the rods; for the one who created this tree desires all who have taken branches from this tree to live. And I too hope that, these rods having received moisture and having been watered with water, the greater part of them will live.”

translation.text:
1 Then the angel of the Lord ordered crowns to be brought. The crowns looked as though they were made from palm leaves. He crowned the men who had handed in rods with shoots and some fruit, and he sent them into the tower.

2 He also sent into the tower those who had handed in green rods with shoots but no fruit, and he gave them seals. 3 Everyone entering the tower wore the same kind of clothing, white as snow. 4 He also sent away those who had returned their rods as green as when they received them, giving them clothing and seals.

5 When the angel had finished, he said to the shepherd, “I am leaving. You must send these people to the walls, according to where each one is worthy to live. Examine their rods carefully before you send them. Be careful that no one slips past you. But if anyone does, I will test that person at the altar.” After saying this to the shepherd, he left.

6 The shepherd said to me, “Let us take everyone’s rods and plant them to see whether any can come back to life.”

I said to him, “Sir, how can these dry rods live?”

7 He answered, “This tree is a willow, a kind of tree that clings strongly to life. If the rods are planted and receive a little moisture, many of them will live. So let us also try pouring water on them. If any comes back to life, I will rejoice over it. But if one does not, no one will be able to say that I failed to care for it.”

8 Then the shepherd told me to call the people in the order in which they had been arranged. They came rank by rank and handed their rods to him. He took the rods and planted them by rank. Then he poured so much water over them that the rods could no longer be seen.

9 After watering the rods, he said to me, “Let us leave and return in a few days to inspect them all. The one who created this tree wants everyone who took a branch from it to live. I too hope that, after receiving this moisture and water, most of these rods will come back to life.”

interpretive_expansions.pob_phrase: to see if any of them will be able to live
interpretive_expansions.rendering: to see whether any can come back to life
interpretive_expansions.claim: “Live” means that the dry cut rods revive after being planted and watered.
evidence: The rods are described as dry before they are planted.
The shepherd expects moisture and water to make many of them live.
alternatives_preserved: The rods’ revival may also symbolize what happens to the people they represent.

spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is substantially clearer and its treatment of the rods’ revival is warranted by the dry rods, planting, and watering in the immediate context. It does not impose a doctrinal explanation on the tower, seals, altar, or rod symbolism. normalized_before.text: Ἐκέλευσε δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος Κυρίου στεφάνους ἐνεχθῆναι. καὶ ἠνέχθησαν στέφανοι ὡσεὶ ἐκ φοινίκων γεγονότες, καὶ ἐστεφάνωσε τοὺς ἄνδρας τοὺς ἐπιδεδωκότας τὰς ῥάβδους τὰς ἐχούσας τὰς παραφυάδας καὶ καρπόν τινα, καὶ ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πύργον. 2. καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους δὲ ἀπέστειλεν εἰς τὸν πύργον, τοὺς τὰς ῥάβδους τὰς χλωρὰς ἐπιδεδωκότας καὶ παραφυάδας ἐχούσας, καρπὸν δὲ μὴ ἐχούσας τὰς παραφυάδας, δοὺς αὐτοῖς σφραγῖδα. 3. ἱματισμὸν δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν πάντες εἶχον λευκὸν ὡσεὶ χιόνα οἱ πορευόμενοι εἰς τὸν πύργον. 4. καὶ τοὺς τὰς ῥάβδους ἐπιδεδωκότας χλωρὰς ὡς ἔλαβον ἀπέλυσε, δοὺς αὐτοῖς ἱματισμὸν [λευκὸν] καὶ σφραγῖδας. 5. μετὰ τὸ ταῦτα τελέσαι τὸν ἄγγελον λέγει τῷ ποιμένι· Ἐγὼ ὑπάγω· σὺ δὲ τούτους ἀπολύσεις εἰς τὰ τείχη, καθὼς ἄξιός ἐστί τις κατοικεῖν. κατανόησον δὲ τὰς ῥάβδους αὐτῶν ἐπιμελῶς, καὶ οὕτως ἀπόλυσον· ἐπιμελῶς δὲ κατανόησον. βλέπε μή τίς σε παρέλθῃ, φησίν. ἐὰν δὲ τίς σε παρέλθῃ, ἐγὼ αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον δοκιμάσω. ταῦτα εἰπὼν τῷ ποιμένι ἀπῆλθε. 6. καὶ μετὰ τὸ ἀπελθεῖν τὸν ἄγγελον λέγει μοι ὁ ποιμήν· Λάβωμεν πάντων τὰς ῥάβδους καὶ φυτεύσωμεν αὐτάς, εἴ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν δυνήσονται ζῆσαι. λέγω αὐτῷ· Κύριε, τὰ ξηρὰ ταῦτα πῶς δύνανται ζῆσαι; 7. ἀποκριθείς μοι λέγει· Τὸ δένδρον τοῦτο ἰτέα ἐστὶ καὶ φιλόζωον τὸ γένος· ἐὰν οὖν φυτευθῶσι καὶ μικρὰν ἰκμάδα λαμβάνωσιν αἱ ῥάβδοι, ζήσονται πολλαὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν· εἶτα δὲ πειράσωμεν καὶ ὕδωρ αὐταῖς παραχέειν. ἐάν τις αὐτῶν δυνηθῇ ζῆσαι, συγχαρήσομαι αὐτῇ· ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ζήσῃ, οὐχ εὑρεθήσομαι ἐγὼ ἀμελής. 8. ἐκέλευσε δέ μοι ὁ ποιμὴν καλέσαι καθὼς τις αὐτῶν ἐστάθη. ἦλθον τάγματα τάγματα, καὶ ἐπεδίδουν τὰς ῥάβδους τῷ ποιμένι. ἐλάμβανε δὲ ὁ ποιμὴν τὰς ῥάβδους, καὶ κατὰ τάγματα ἐφύτευσεν αὐτάς, καὶ μετὰ τὸ φυτεῦσαι ὕδωρ αὐταῖς πολὺ παρέχεεν, ὥστε ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος μὴ φαίνεσθαι τὰς ῥάβδους. 9. καὶ μετὰ τὸ ποτίσαι αὐτὸν τὰς ῥάβδους λέγει μοι· Ἄγωμεν, καὶ μετ' ὀλίγας ἡμέρας ἐπανέλθωμεν καὶ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τὰς ῥάβδους πάσας· ὁ γὰρ κτίσας τὸ δένδρον τοῦτο θέλει πάντας ζῆν τοὺς λαβόντας ἐκ τοῦ δένδρου τούτου κλάδους. ἐλπίζω δὲ κἀγὼ ὅτι λαβόντα τὰ ῥαβδία ταῦτα ἰκμάδα καὶ ποτισθέντα ὕδατι ζήσονται τὸ πλεῖστον μέρος αὐτῶν.
